Prevention: Improve the air flow in the field to reduce humidity and reduce appearance of disease
Eliminate any wild grapes in nearby fields
Prune and destroy any previously infected shoots in the dormant period
Make sure you get clean seed, clean vines so that they are grafted healthily onto root stock, that is from a reputed and registered dealer in the beginning
Collecting of infected leaf and weeds in
Shovel the soil to plough under the crop residues to interrupt the disease’s lifecycle
Monitoring: Monitoring should be done once a week.
Monitoring is done on leaf and grape.
It is possible to see round spots on stems and berries, that become larger and with a grey centre with a raised on the edges
You can also see spots on the leaves, again round with grey centre that eventually dries and looks like a shot hole
Young leaves are more susceptible to infection
Direct Control: Pruning can be done to cut the infected parts in
December, be sure to remove any mummified fruits or diseased tendrils
Collecting of the residue after pruning and remove from the orchard
For pruning, the tools should be sterilized with salt solution and alcohol; or washing up liquid
Urea spray 1kg/20 liter water in autumn season
Restrictions: When using a pesticide, always wear protective clothing and follow the instructions on the product label, such as dosage
During the use of pesticides, prevent children and animals from entering the field and do not eat drink or smoke whilst using chemicals of any kind
Change your clothes and wash your body and face after using chemicals
Keep pesticides out of reach of children
Using of lime sulfur 1 liter of lime sulfur per 9 liter of water.
Lime sulphur is slightly hazardous; Class
III; may be harmful if swallowed or absorbed through the skin
Using of lime sulfur must be done in
Mancozeb or chlorothalonil @ 3-4 g/litre of water
Unlikely to present acute hazard in normal use
